claims.text: Astoria Boulevard North & Hoyt Avenue North had 78 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 7 pedestrians injured, 3 cyclists injured and 1 person killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $5.3 million a year (injury crashes only: deaths are not valued in this figure).
21% of crashes here had “following too closely” recorded as a contributing factor, against 6% at the city's priority junctions.
11% of crashes here had “passing or lane usage improper” recorded as a contributing factor, against 5% at the city's priority junctions.
7% of crashes here had “unsafe lane changing” recorded as a contributing factor, against 2% at the city's priority junctions.
Held up on later years: “following too closely” was recorded in 24% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 6% at the city's priority junctions (found by the AI analyst).
Held up on later years: only people in vehicles hurt and it happened in the daytime in 24% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 15% at the city's priority junctions (found by the greedy search).

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 2.3 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $801,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 1.2 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $417,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red; the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11 is responsible for BKLYN/QUEENS EXP (I 278) (owner recorded in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory).
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Astoria Boulevard North, Hoyt Avenue North (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 22, New York City Council; Queens Community Board 1.
A request letter to the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11 and the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11; the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 22, New York City Council; Queens Community Board 1
Subject: Request for safety review: Astoria Boulevard North & Hoyt Avenue North

Dear colleagues at NYSDOT Region 11 and NYC DOT,

We are writing about the junction of Astoria Boulevard North & Hoyt Avenue North.

For the roads you are responsible for [NYSDOT Region 11: BKLYN/QUEENS EXP (I 278); NYC DOT: Astoria Boulevard North, Hoyt Avenue North], we ask you to carry out a safety study at this location and consider fixes.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 213 crashes, including 78 injury crashes. 7 pedestrians and 3 cyclists were reported injured, and 1 person was killed. This location is a New York City priority location. In the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), the yearly cost of the harm is $5.3 million. No safety work is recorded in this period [last recorded project: Astoria Boulevard at 31st and 33rd Streets, 2015].

Two low-cost signal measures could help reduce injury crashes, subject to an on-site check:

- longer yellow signal times, where an entry on yellow or red must be checked on site. On this record it is estimated to prevent about 4.2 injury crashes per year (about $1,453,000 in harm avoided per year).
- reflective backplates on the traffic signals, where an entry on yellow or red must be checked on site. Estimated to prevent about 2.3 injury crashes per year (about $801,000 per year).

Where measured in this city, a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green) was linked to fewer pedestrian injuries: where the city installed it at 1,651 intersections, pedestrian injury crashes fell 17% (95% interval 11% to 22%) compared with intersections that got it later; a stricter check against fake programs is less certain. This also needs a site check for a turning movement.

Please advise on next steps.

Yours sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]
